## 1. Problem

The founder, 2026-10-20, in chat, verbatim: "the website seems a bit confusing, so a few pages and everything. So fix that up." The orchestrator walked the live site (flowersoverseas.com, release 770c63a4, `noindex`) and listed twelve findings (C1 to C12, work order `wo-spec-043`). The spec writer re-checked each on the live pages and in the code on 2026-10-20; §1.1 records what holds.

The site makes a visitor answer three questions before it answers theirs: **which country am I shopping for, can I order, and why did the prices just vanish?** The header mixes three browse models (a country shop, country-less category hubs with no prices, country-less occasion hubs with no prices), so one click from a priced Poland page lands on a price-less page that asks for the destination again. The ordering state is said two or three times per page in different words ("Guide · not delivering yet", "P.S. Ordering opens soon", "(not yet)"), seven times in a row on the destinations block, and some public lines read like notes to ourselves ("Our picks until real orders start.", "Photography to supply"). Ranking stays priority 1 (`CLAUDE.md`): every fix keeps every indexable hub, URL, canonical, sitemap and hreflang as it is.

## 2. Scope

- **A. The header knows the destination from the URL.** On a page whose URL names a destination with a shop, the header's shop items (Our selection, Bouquets, Roses, Plants, Birthday, Sympathy) link to that destination's own priced pages, in the server HTML, per URL, the same for every visitor. Everywhere else they link exactly where they do today.
- **B. One head for every country listing.** Under the H1, one destination line ("Where is it going? Poland · change destination", reviewed keys) whose link leads to the hub of the same thing; one ordering-state line; no "P.S." mark, no state eyebrow.
- **C. The state said once per block.** The home's Destinations block and the destinations hub print the shared state once when every destination shares it.
- **D. Can I order? on the home's first screen.** While no destination takes orders, the not-open state text sits in the first viewport beside the sentence form.
- **E. Chips grouped by kind.** On the shop root, and inside the country category's "Categories" disclosure, the chips for what it is come first and the occasion chips follow, each group under a reviewed heading.
- **F. No empty boxes up front, no internal caption.** In every product list, products with an approved photograph come before products without one; a placeholder box carries no words; every card of a grid is visible after a real scroll and when printed.
- **G. Copy that sounds like a shop.** The home row heading, the count line's noun, the destinations hub intro, and the occasions index caption at every width (§7 table).
- **H. No eyebrow repeats the trail.** No eyebrow on a listing or hub page equals a label of that page's breadcrumb.

## 3. Non-goals

- **The language popup (C3).** Spec 003 §14 A-founder-2026-10-19d and spec 004 §14 A-founder-2026-10-19d decide it; the orchestrator plans their one build row. The header's "English | English (UK) | EUR" density is TASK-136's.
- **Card price lines and the example label (C5, part of C4).** Spec 004 §14 A-founder-2026-10-19b and spec 008 §14 A-founder-2026-10-19b. Its build row does not exist yet; §12 puts it beside 043's card task.
- **The trust, help and legal pages and their footer links (C7), and `faq.allTopicsPending`.** Spec 041, TASK-182 (PR 270) and TASK-183: the pending sentence leaves the home when the help page is published (spec 041 AC-21).
- **"24/7 —" in `company.support.hours`.** TASK-238 (blocked on copy).
- **The three mismatched photographs.** TASK-250.
- **The words "Ordering opens soon", Poland `demo`, the finder's "soon" marks and the cutoff gate.** TASK-239 (spec 007 §14 A-founder-2026-10-14c). 043 builds on it and changes no word it sets.
- **Sort and chip placement above the grid.** TASK-241 (PR 235). 043 only groups the chips it places.
- **The ranking line** (`shop.toolbar.disclosure`). It stays, word for word and visible, in TASK-241's toolbar: `plan/07` §2.1 keeps a ranking statement on listings and spec 008 AC-9 asserts it.
- **A remembered destination** (cookie or storage). The destination stays in the URL (`plan/03` §1, `plan/01` §4.4); §13 Q2.
- **A destination switch that keeps the same product** across countries (`plan/03` §1 "Change country"). The change link goes to the hub of the same category or occasion; same-entity switching is a later spec.
- **Hub cards as links.** Hub cards stay non-links (spec 008 AC-12 on a destination-less page); the destination rows above them are the way in.
- **Motion values and photo loading.** Spec 042 (PR 284, "soft photo loading") owns motion 11's look; 043 adds only the print rule and the real-scroll proof.
- **The two gift-set prices** found in §1.1: money, seed data, its own row.

## 4. User stories

- As a **buyer on a Poland page**, when I click Roses in the header I see Poland's roses with prices, so I never lose the country I chose.
- As a **buyer**, I see once, in plain words, whether I can order and that every price is the price I pay, so I do not read the same warning three times.
- As a **buyer on the home**, I learn in the first screen that ordering opens soon, before I fill the sentence in.
- As a **buyer on a country page**, I can see which country I am shopping for and change it in one click, and the change takes me to the same kind of flowers for another country.
- As a **buyer scanning the shop**, I find "what it is" and "what it is for" as two short groups instead of one list of twenty.
- As **Googlebot**, I find the same hubs, URLs, canonicals, sitemaps and hreflang as before, every link answers 200, and every document is the same for every visitor.
- As the **founder**, I approve one short copy list, and the public site stops sounding like a draft.

## 5. Design

### 5.1 Data model changes

None. No table, column, migration or rollback. Everything reads existing data: the destination in the URL, `listingExists()`, the hub destination rows `listingView()` already builds, `categories.json`'s `kind`, `media_asset.review_state`, `deliveryDatesOpen()` / `anyDeliveryDatesOpen()`.

### 5.2 API / server actions / jobs / events

No route, action, job or event. Two pure functions in `src/modules/catalog`, exported from its barrel, zod-free (inputs are already parsed views):

- `destinationShopLinks(locale, iso2): Promise<ShopNavLinks | undefined>` — for each header shop item, the href in destination `iso2`, or `undefined` when the destination has no shop root in `locale`. The rule (one source of truth with the hubs):
  - Our selection → the destination's shop root.
  - Bouquets, Roses, Plants (category hubs `bouquet`, `roses`, `plant`) → the href that category hub's own destination list gives for `iso2`; else the shop root.
  - Birthday, Sympathy (occasion hubs) → the href that occasion hub's own destination list gives for `iso2`; else the shop root.
  - Occasions, Destinations → not in the result (unchanged everywhere).
- `photoFirst<T extends { photo: { kind: string } }>(items: readonly T[]): T[]` — a stable partition: items whose photo is an approved asset first, in input order, then the rest, in input order.

`ShopNavLinks` is a plain record keyed by the `categories.ts` row id. No new zod schema crosses a boundary.

### 5.3 UI

The `/design` pass draws every state below at 1440 × 900 and 390 × 844 before `/plan-tasks` (§12).

**A. The header (C2).**
- **Country context.** A page is in the context of destination X when its URL carries X's slug: the country shop root, a country category, a country occasion, a product page, and X's guide (`/{locale}/{destinations}/{x}`). Checkout, tracking, info and legal pages carry no context.
- **In context, with a shop root for X in that locale:** the six shop items link as `destinationShopLinks()` says, on the desktop row and in the phone Menu. Labels, order, styles, Occasions, Destinations and Send flowers are unchanged.
- **Out of context, or no shop root:** every item links exactly as today (`site-links.ts`; Our selection to `DEMO_DESTINATION_ISO2`'s shop root).
- **How it stays static.** The row is resolved per route without reading request headers, cookies or the client path, in the way the `@notice` and `@switcher` parallel-route slots already do (`src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx` L193 to L204). No client JavaScript is added. The mechanism is the implementer's within these constraints.
- No item ever links to a URL that is not 200 (spec 004 AC-14).

**B. The country listing head (C1, C4, C10).** On the shop root, the country category and the country occasion page, every page number:
- Breadcrumb (unchanged), H1 (unchanged).
- **The destination line**, directly under the H1: `product.destination.label` ("Where is it going?"), the country name, and `product.destination.change` ("change destination") as a link. Its target is the hub whose own destination list links this page (the inverse of A's mapping): a category hub before an occasion hub where both do; the destinations hub where none does, and always on the shop root. Same component and look as the product page's destination control (spec 009), drawn by `/design` for the listing.
- **One state line, page 1 only.** While ordering is not open in X (`deliveryDatesOpen(X)` false): `shop.root.demoNotice` ("Ordering opens soon. Every price here is the price you will pay, with VAT and delivery included."), as plain text. No separate state eyebrow, no `shop.note.mark` ("P.S."), no `shop.note.label`. While ordering is open: the state line `destinations.state.deliveringNow` as today and no demo notice.
- On a phone the country occasion page keeps the note's place after the grid (spec 008 §14 A-founder-2026-10-18c), without the mark.
- The occasion hub's `shop.hub.noMoney` sentence renders once, as plain text, without the "P.S." mark.

**C. The destinations block (C11).** On the home's Destinations block and on the destinations hub: when every listed destination has the same state, the state text renders once, as the block's caption, and no row carries it. When states differ (a destination opens), each row carries its own, as spec 007 AC-33 says.

**D. The home's first screen (C1).** While `anyDeliveryDatesOpen()` is false, the not-open state text (the key TASK-239 sets to "Ordering opens soon") renders as one line inside the hero's sentence section, visible in the first viewport at 1440 × 900 and 390 × 844. It disappears, as data, the moment any destination opens. No date is printed (§13 Q3).

**E. Chips grouped by kind (C6).** Wherever the shop root's chip row (or tiles) and the country category's "Categories" disclosure (TASK-241) list categories:
- group 1, the categories of kind `productType` and `flowerType`, under `shop.root.tilesHeading` ("By what it is");
- group 2, the categories of kind `occasion`, under `home.occasions.eyebrow` ("Shop by occasion");
- within a group, today's order; the set of links, their hrefs and the current-category mark unchanged; native markup, no script.
- Below `md` on the shop root: one horizontal scroller per group, or one scroller with group 2 after group 1 behind its heading, as `/design` draws; spec 004 rebound AC-34 (first-row prices inside the first viewport) still holds.

**F. Photographs (C8, C12).**
- **Photo-first.** Every product list (country listings in "Our order", hub grids, the home row, the product page's related row) passes its items through `photoFirst()` after spec 005's order. Price sorts are unchanged. Pagination and `ItemList` follow the new order (spec 008 AC-17 stays equal to the rendered cards).
- **A wordless placeholder.** A product without an approved photograph shows the `--color-photo` box with no caption, `aria-hidden`, on cards and in the product gallery. The card's name and price stay. No buyer page renders "Photography to supply". Placeholder keys no renderer reads any more are deleted (i18n unused-key rule).
- **Visible after a real scroll; visible in print.** Motion 11 (image fade) and motion 12 (section reveal) start `opacity: 0` only on screen: under `@media print` every element they hold is at full opacity. A visitor who scrolls the grid sees every photograph. The values of both motions are spec 042's and spec 004's.

**G. Copy (C4, C9).** The four value changes of §7's table. On the occasions index, `occasionsIndex.datedCaption` is displayed at every width wherever the "next six" block shows (today it is hidden below `md`).

**H. Eyebrows (C10).** On the country listings, the category hubs, the occasion hubs, the occasions index and the destinations hub, no eyebrow's text equals, ignoring case, any label of the same page's breadcrumb. Today that removes the occasion hub's "Occasions" eyebrow; the country listings lose theirs by B.

**States.** Empty listing (spec 008 AC-8): unchanged, no destination line or state line beyond what AC-8 prints. Error and not-found pages: header out of context. JS off: everything above renders (no island). Demo vs live: B, C and D read `deliveryDatesOpen` / `anyDeliveryDatesOpen` only.

### 5.4 Rendering and caching

Unchanged per `plan/01` §3: home, hubs, listings and guides stay ISR with today's tags and `revalidate` (spec 008 AC-22, spec 007 A8). The header slot renders at build and revalidation like the page under it; no `headers()`, `cookies()` or `searchParams` read is added to a prerendered route. No `Vary`, no `Set-Cookie`. No tag is added: the header's targets change only with the catalogue, whose existing `catalog:{country}` invalidation already re-renders every page in that country's context.

## 6. SEO considerations (mandatory)

- **Indexability, canonicals, hreflang, sitemaps, robots:** unchanged on every page type. No URL is created, removed or renamed (`plan/02` §4.1). `pnpm seo:validate` and the sitemap snapshots are equal before and after (T-06).
- **URL pattern:** destination stays in the path (`plan/02` §4.2); locale stays in the prefix; nothing reads IP, cookie or `Accept-Language` (ADR-0006).
- **Internal links (`plan/02` §11).** Out-of-context pages (home, hubs, info pages, the occasions index, the destinations hub) keep linking the five hubs from the header. On in-context pages the header links move from the hubs to the destination's own category and occasion pages, which is the `plan/02` §11 direction (authority to country money pages), and the new "change destination" link on every country listing points back at the matching hub. Every hub stays at crawl depth ≤ 3 from each locale home (T-06). While the country pages are `noindex,follow` (ADR-0007), the hubs' inbound links from indexable pages are unchanged.
- **Structured data:** `BreadcrumbList` unchanged. `ItemList` order follows photo-first and stays equal to the rendered cards (spec 008 AC-17). No `Product` or `Offer` on listings (spec 008 AC-18).
- **Thin content:** lines removed are repeats (a second state line, a "P.S." mark, a basis line); each page keeps its H1, lede and grid. The destinations hub keeps its intro, shortened by one sentence (§7).
- **Server HTML for everyone:** all changes are in the server HTML, the same for every visitor of a URL; no client-only content, no cloaking risk.
- **CWV:** no client JavaScript and no image added; three text nodes removed on listings. LCP element unchanged (the first card's photo on listings; photo-first guarantees it is a real photograph whenever the list has one). CLS unchanged. The home's added line sits inside the hero's reserved block (T-08 measures the first-screen fit at 390 × 844).

## 7. i18n considerations (mandatory)

- **No new message key.** Every new element reuses a key reviewed by the founder: `product.destination.label`, `product.destination.change`, `shop.root.tilesHeading`, `home.occasions.eyebrow`, `shop.root.demoNotice`, `occasionsIndex.datedCaption`, TASK-239's not-open state key. Copy headroom is zero (`en-gb` 4.98 % of spec 003 A17's 5 %).
- **Changed values (founder copy batch; §13 Q4).** Each ships with the founder's own `record-approval` run **on the same PR branch, before merge**, so `main` never holds them unreviewed (spec 003 A17 clause 5).

| Key | Today (`en`) | Proposed (`en`) |
|---|---|---|
| `home.trending.heading` | Popular `<em>`choices`</em>` | Our `<em>`selection`</em>` |
| `shop.toolbar.count` | `{count, plural, one {# bouquet} other {# bouquets}}` | `{noun, select, plant {{count, plural, one {# plant} other {# plants}}} arrangement {{count, plural, one {# arrangement} other {# arrangements}}} other {{count, plural, one {# bouquet} other {# bouquets}}}}` |
| `shop.toolbar.summary` | `… bouquets} · page {page} of {pageCount}` | the same select as `count`, then ` · page {page} of {pageCount}` |
| `destinationsHub.intro` | … "We write the guide first and open delivery after it. Where we are not delivering yet, this page says so in the same words on every row." | the same text without its last sentence |

  `noun` is the category's noun the tile count already uses (`shop.root.tileCount`); the shop root and occasion pages pass `other`. `en-gb` inherits; `de` and `pl` (hidden) get drafts by the existing draft policy.
- **Deleted keys** (no renderer left): `home.trending.basis`, `shop.note.mark`, `shop.note.label`, and each `media.placeholder.*` key no renderer reads after §5.3 F. Deleting a reviewed counted key raises the unreviewed share slightly (about +0.01 point each on today's catalogue), so each PR prints `i18n:check`'s `en-gb` share before and after, and stays inside the line on its head SHA.
- **Formatting:** unchanged (`formatMoney`, `formatDate`, ICU plurals). The count line's noun is an ICU `select` (no string concatenation).
- **RTL:** the destination line, the chip groups and the block caption use logical properties only; `/ar-XB` mirrors them (visual baselines, T-14).
- **Addresses, phones:** none rendered by this spec. The help number is data in `company.ts` (§13 Q7).
- **Review gating and `noindex`:** unchanged; spec 003 AC-24's line is checked on every 043 PR (T-15).

## 8. Compliance considerations (mandatory)

- **Data flows:** none added. No cookie, storage, request or analytics event. RoPA unchanged (the PR notes "no new processing").
- **Price display (`CLAUDE.md`, `plan/07` §2.1, spec 008 AC-6, AC-7):** every country-scoped card keeps one all-in price; destination-less pages keep no money; `shop.root.demoNotice` keeps "every price here is the price you will pay, with VAT and delivery included" on page 1 of every country listing. The home's added line states only that ordering opens soon.
- **Ranking transparency (`plan/07` §2.1 Omnibus row):** `shop.toolbar.disclosure` unchanged and visible above the grid. Photo-first is a presentation rule that ranks by no commercial criterion; the disclosure ("the order we chose ourselves … not a ranking by sales, by popularity or by payment") stays true.
- **Honesty (`plan/10` §3, spec 004 A5):** no claim is added. A placeholder shows no image we do not have and now no internal words. The "Our selection" heading claims curation, not popularity, so it needs no basis line. No banned word (relay, partner, …) is added; the voice scan stays green.
- **Geo-blocking (EU 2018/302, ADR-0006):** every destination's pages stay reachable from anywhere; the header follows the URL, never the visitor's country; nothing redirects.
- **Post-purchase framing and no partner language (founder rulings 2026-10-14):** untouched; 043 changes no checkout, confirmation, tracking or email surface.
- **Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA, EAA):** the destination line's link has a visible label naming its action; chip groups are labelled (`aria-labelledby` or a visible heading); the placeholder box is `aria-hidden` and the card's name stays the accessible text; nothing hidden by motion is hidden in print; axe zero serious/critical (T-14).
- **Logs/PII:** nothing logged.

## 9. Acceptance criteria

The "crawl set" is spec 004 AC-14's (the shown locales plus `/`). "Today's data" is the committed registries with TASK-239 merged. "The open fixture" is spec 007 AC-33's (Poland open: operations, an active-florist provider, `status: "live"`).

- **AC-1** On `/en/poland/flowers`, `/en/poland/flowers/roses`, `/en/poland/product/amber-hour`, `/en/send-flowers-to/poland`, `/en/france/flowers` and their `en-gb` counterparts, with JavaScript off, the header row at 1440 × 900 and the phone Menu at 390 × 844 link: Our selection to that destination's shop root; Bouquets, Roses and Plants to the href the matching category hub's destination list gives for that destination; Birthday and Sympathy to the href the matching occasion hub's destination list gives for it. Occasions, Destinations and Send flowers keep today's hrefs.
- **AC-2** Under a fixture where one of those destination pages does not exist in the locale, that item links to the destination's shop root. Over the crawl set plus every in-context page in `en` and `en-gb`, no header or Menu link answers other than 200.
- **AC-3** On `/en`, `/en-gb`, every category hub, every occasion hub, the occasions index, the destinations hub, and a 404 page, the header row's and Menu's hrefs are equal to the committed baseline taken from `main` before the change.

## 11. Observability

No event, log or alert is added. `plan/04` analytics stays off (no GA4 id). After the indexing flip, Search Console internal-link counts per hub are the signal that the hubs kept their inbound links; `/seo-audit` on the hub set is part of that flip's runbook, not this spec.

## 12. Rollout

- **Flags:** none. B, C and D read `deliveryDatesOpen` / `anyDeliveryDatesOpen`, so they change by data when a destination opens.
- **Design first.** `/design` on this spec draws, in `docs/design/wireframes/`: the country listing head (shop root, country category, country occasion; desktop and mobile; demo and open states); the occasion hub head without the eyebrow; the home first screen with the state line; the home Destinations block and the destinations hub with one caption and with mixed states; the shop root chip groups and the grouped "Categories" disclosure; a grid with a wordless placeholder. The header needs no drawing (labels and look unchanged).
- **Copy:** the founder approves §7's table with this spec, and records it on each copy-bearing PR's branch before merge (A17 clause 5).
- **Order and dependencies:**
  1. TASK-239 (spec 007 A-founder-2026-10-14c) and TASK-241 (PR 235) merge first: 043 builds on their words and their toolbar.
  2. Spec 004 §14 A-founder-2026-10-19b's build row (C5) is planned by the orchestrator and goes to the **same agent and PR as task 3** below (both edit `ProductCard` and the listing grids).
  3. Spec 003/004 A-founder-2026-10-19d's build row (C3) is independent of 043.
- **Task split (siblings that share a component go together):**
  1. **Header in context** — AC-1, AC-2, AC-3, AC-4, AC-6 (T-01 to T-04, T-06). `destinationShopLinks()`, the per-route header slot, `site-links.ts` unchanged. Keeps the breaker (internal links, an SEO gate, caching).
  2. **Listing heads, chips and the eyebrow rule** — AC-5, AC-7, AC-11, AC-12, AC-16, AC-17, AC-18, AC-19 (count-line half) (T-05, T-07, T-11, T-12, T-16, T-17, T-18, T-19). After TASK-239 and TASK-241. Keeps the breaker (listing links, price-display copy).
  3. **Product lists and photographs** — AC-13, AC-14, AC-15 (T-13 to T-15), with spec 004 A-founder-2026-10-19b's row in the same PR. Keeps the breaker (`ItemList` order, money display on cards).
  4. **Home and destinations** — AC-8, AC-9, AC-10, AC-19 (home and hub half) (T-08, T-09, T-10, T-19). After TASK-239. Review-only unless the reviewer finds price or SEO text touched (the heading feeds no `<title>`).
  5. AC-20 (T-20) is the design PR's.
- **Rollback:** each task is one revert; no data, no migration.

## 13. Open questions

Each has a recommended default; "043 defaults" answers all of them.

- **Q1. The browse model (C2).** (A) The header follows the destination in the URL, as §5.3 A. (B) A slimmer header: Bouquets, Roses, Plants, Birthday and Sympathy leave the header for the footer's Sending group, and the header keeps Our selection, Occasions, Destinations and Send flowers. **Default A**: it keeps the shop-like header you asked for on 2026-09-09 and fixes the jump out of Poland; B is simpler to build but takes away the items you found dead on 2026-10-03 and had made into links.
- **Q2. Remember the chosen destination** in a cookie, so the home and hubs also point at it? **Default no**: the URL already carries it on every country page, and a cookie would either split the cached pages (bad for ranking) or need extra script.
- **Q3. An opening date.** Print a month ("Ordering opens in November") instead of "soon"? **Default no**, until you can name a date you will keep.
- **Q4. The copy list in §7** (the heading "Our selection", the count line by noun, the hub intro without its last sentence). **Default: approved as written.**
- **Q5. The "P.S." device** leaves the listings and the occasion hubs entirely (it is the letter-home mark of the 2026-10-03 look). **Default yes**: on a shop page it reads as an afterthought in front of the most important line.
- **Q6. Products without a photograph (C8).** (A) Photographed products first, and the empty box shows no words. (B) Hide them from every list until a photograph is approved (the plants page goes from 8 to 6). **Default A**: no page, count or category changes; the two plants come back to the front the day their photographs are approved.
- **Q7. The US WhatsApp number** `+1 (213) 592-5150` in the header. **Default: keep it until you have a European WhatsApp number** (Polish or Dutch), then change it as data in `src/config/company.ts`; no code change either way.
- **Q8. The destinations block (C11)** says "Ordering opens soon" once for all seven instead of on every row. **Default yes.**
